selected_leaf.question: Does any documented non-mutating GitHub REST, GraphQL, release-attestation, or current-repository surface expose deleted immutable-release tag-name reservations or a maximum immutable generation after repository delete/recreate and loss of role-local newest-version state?
selected_leaf.scope: One bounded official-GitHub documentation leaf only; no destructive repository/release/tag probe, no other-worker state, no downstream/O inputs, no external hosted compute.

public_sources.title: Immutable releases - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed: Published immutable release tags cannot be moved; after deleting the immutable release the tag may be deleted but the same tag name cannot be reused. GitHub explicitly states the protection survives deleting a repository and creating a new repository with the same name. The release also gets a release attestation containing tag, commit SHA, and assets.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for releases and release assets - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed: The documented release endpoint family exposes list/create/latest/get-by-tag/get/update/delete for releases and asset operations; no documented deleted-release or reserved-immutable-tag enumeration endpoint appeared in the bounded endpoint family.

public_sources.title: Releases / Repositories - GitHub GraphQL reference
public_sources.observed: The Release object exposes current release fields including immutable, tag and tagName. The Repository reference exposes release(tagName) and releases connections for releases dependent on that repository; no deleted-release/reserved-tag history field appeared in the bounded reference surfaces.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for repositories - immutable releases setting
public_sources.observed: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/immutable-releases reports only current enabled state and whether owner policy enforces it; it does not document a reservation list, prior generations, or a maximum retired generation.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for artifact attestations / Managing attestation lifecycle - GitHub Docs
public_sources.observed: Organization attestation lookup is keyed by subject digest; the lifecycle documentation states that a deleted attestation can no longer be found on GitHub. The bounded docs did not expose lookup by deleted immutable tag reservation or a monotonic maximum-generation index.

known_old_tag_name.observation: GitHub documents that the provider still rejects reuse after deletion/resurrection, but the tested current release/GraphQL/settings surfaces expose current objects/settings rather than a reservation-status record for an absent tag.
known_old_tag_name.inference_guard: This is a bounded documentation/API-surface classification, not a live destructive proof that every undocumented/internal endpoint is absent.

unknown_old_tag_name.observation: No tested REST/GraphQL/settings/attestation surface enumerates deleted immutable tag-name reservations. Without a prior tag name or subject digest, the hidden anti-reuse set is not reconstructible from the bounded documented surfaces.

deleted_release_absent_from_ordinary_lis.observation: The documented release collection describes releases in the repository; the bounded endpoint catalog contains delete but no deleted-release-history/list-reservations operation.

recreated_repository_same_name.observation: GitHub explicitly guarantees old immutable tag names remain non-reusable after repository resurrection, proving provider-side retained authority state exists beyond the current repository object. The tested surfaces do not expose that state as a monotonic floor.

immutable_setting_disabled_reenabled.observation: The current setting endpoint reveals only current enablement/enforcement. The bounded docs do not state that toggling the setting exposes or erases the hidden historical reservation set; no acceptance inference is made.

release_attestation.observation: A release attestation can prove a known published release, but documented organization lookup requires a subject digest and deleted attestations cease to be findable. No tested tag-reservation or maximum-generation enumeration route is documented.

rate_limit_or_read_interruption.observation: With role-local newest-version state lost, an interrupted provider read yields no reconstructible maximum-generation proof. This leaf performs no mutative probe and would checkpoint rather than guess or retry in-run.

mutative_future_witness_probe.observation: Attempting to create candidate tag names could reveal reservation membership but mutates provider state and consumes future witness names; it is outside this leaf and is not an accepted discovery mechanism.

result.new_positive_evidence: GitHub's immutable-release anti-reuse state is provider-retained across release deletion and same-name repository resurrection, so the provider has a stronger hidden tombstone/reservation than ordinary current repository state.
result.new_falsification: Across the bounded documented REST release catalog, GraphQL Release/Repository surfaces, current immutable-release settings, and digest-keyed attestation surfaces, no non-mutating provider API was found that enumerates deleted immutable-release tag reservations or yields a maximum immutable generation after both current repository history and role-local newest-version state are gone.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A provider-enforced, non-mutating, statelessly discoverable monotonic retirement floor (or complete historical reservation enumeration) that survives repository delete/recreate without requiring a known deleted tag/digest, mutative probing, paid/finite quota, external hosted coordination, or local newest-version state.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.reason_quota_zero_not_proven: This leaf did not establish universal entitlement/availability of immutable-release or historical-attestation features at zero optional paid/trial quota, and no accepted mechanism was found.

scope_guard: Absence is claimed only for the bounded official documented surfaces inspected in this invocation. It is not a claim that GitHub has no internal, future, enterprise-only, or undocumented historical index.
continuation: Part91: execute exactly one bounded official-GitHub historical-audit surface leaf. Test whether organization/repository audit-log or provider activity history can non-mutatingly reconstruct immutable-release publish/delete/tag-reservation generations across repository delete/recreate and local-state loss. Required negatives: finite retention window, repository-id/name reuse, missing immutable-release-specific event fields, org/enterprise/paid entitlement, export/API rate-limit interruption, deleted organization/repository history, unknown prior tag, no mutative probe, zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota and zero incremental cost. Accept only if the history is provider-enforced, complete enough to derive a monotonic retirement floor, survives resurrection for the needed horizon, is statelessly discoverable, and has no paid/finite-quota or external-executor dependency; otherwise persist the exact retention/entitlement/completeness gap and choose the next provider-side authority leaf for the following invocation.
